Capturing Your UK Touring Adventures

Action cameras have revolutionised how riders document their tours. From sweeping Highland vistas to twisty Welsh mountain passes, modern cameras capture stunning footage that lets you relive and share your adventures. They also serve a practical purpose — video evidence is invaluable in the event of an accident or insurance claim.

Camera Types

  • Standard action cameras — Traditional rectangular cameras like the GoPro Hero series. Wide-angle lens, excellent stabilisation, and proven reliability in all conditions.
  • 360-degree cameras — Cameras like the Insta360 X4 that capture everything around them. You choose the viewing angle in post-production, meaning you never miss a shot.
  • Modular cameras — Systems like the DJI Action series that can be configured in different ways for different mounting positions.

Best Cameras for Moto Touring 2026

GoPro Hero 13 — The benchmark action camera with HyperSmooth stabilisation that eliminates motorcycle vibration. 5.3K resolution, excellent low-light performance, and a waterproof body that handles British rain without a case.

Insta360 X4 — 360-degree capture at 8K lets you reframe shots after the ride. The invisible selfie stick effect creates dramatic third-person footage. Excellent for scenery-focused touring content.

DJI Osmo Action 5 Pro — Excellent image stabilisation and colour science. The magnetic mounting system is quick to attach and remove. Vertical shooting mode works well for social media content.

GoPro Mini — A compact, lightweight option for riders who want minimal helmet weight. Reduced feature set but still captures excellent footage with stabilisation.

Mounting Options

Chin mount — The most popular position giving a natural rider's eye view. Use a curved adhesive mount on the chin bar of your helmet. Check that it does not interfere with your visor mechanism.

Side mount — Mounted on the side of the helmet. Creates interesting angled footage but adds wind noise and can catch in crosswinds at speed.

Handlebar mount — Fixed to the handlebars for a stable forward view. Avoids added helmet weight but captures more vibration than helmet-mounted cameras.

Always check local laws regarding helmet-mounted cameras. In the UK, there is no specific law against helmet cameras, but any mounting must not compromise the helmet's structural integrity or safety certification.

Battery Management on Tour

Action camera batteries typically last 1-2 hours of continuous recording. Carry at least three spare batteries on a touring day and charge them via USB from your motorcycle or a power bank during stops. Some riders wire a USB power cable directly from the bike to the camera for continuous recording without battery concerns. keyTakeaways: Standard action cameras like the GoPro Hero 13 are the reliable all-rounders with excellent stabilisation.
360-degree cameras such as the Insta360 X4 let you reframe every shot after the ride.
A chin mount gives the most natural rider's-eye view with the least wind noise.
Footage doubles as valuable video evidence for accident and insurance claims.
Carry at least three spare batteries or hard-wire USB power for continuous recording.

pros: Captures scenery and relives tours long after the ride ends.
Provides video evidence that can settle insurance disputes.

cons: Batteries typically last only one to two hours of recording.

faq.q: Are helmet cameras legal in the UK?
faq.a: There is no specific UK law banning helmet-mounted cameras. However, any mount must not compromise the helmet's structural integrity or safety certification. Use a proper adhesive mount designed for the job rather than drilling or bolting anything into the shell, and check that the camera does not foul your visor mechanism.

faq.q: Where is the best place to mount an action camera?
faq.a: The chin mount is the most popular position, giving a natural rider's-eye view with minimal wind noise. A curved adhesive mount on the chin bar works well as long as it does not interfere with the visor. Side mounts create interesting angles but add wind noise and can catch crosswinds, while a handlebar mount avoids helmet weight but records more vibration.

faq.q: How do I keep the camera recording all day?
faq.a: Action camera batteries typically last one to two hours of continuous recording, so carry at least three spares and charge them via USB during stops. Many touring riders wire a USB power cable directly from the bike to the camera, which removes battery anxiety entirely and lets you record the whole day without swapping batteries at the roadside.

faq.q: Do I need a 360 camera or a standard one?
faq.a: A standard camera like the GoPro Hero 13 is simpler, has better battery life and produces sharp footage straight out of the camera. A 360 camera such as the Insta360 X4 films everything around you so you choose the angle later in editing, which is brilliant for scenic touring content but means more time at the computer and larger files.

Action cameras are built to cope with the vibration a helmet or bike mount subjects them to, unlike phone cameras which can suffer optical stabilisation damage. Modern electronic stabilisation such as GoPro HyperSmooth actively cancels motorcycle vibration in the footage, so shots look smooth even on a rough B-road.
